title: Shell-line segmenter ignores a backslash-escaped quote outside quotes, which can hide a cd from shell following
outcome: engram_shell_commands (src/engram_check_paths.rs) splits a line at `;`, `&&`, `||` and groups only outside quotes, but it tracks quotes without honouring a backslash escape outside them. In bash, `echo \"; cd /x; echo \"` runs `cd /x`. The segmenter reads `\"` as opening a double quote and so treats `; cd /x; echo ` as quoted text. The cd is then invisible both to the followed path (engram_shell_move) and to the lost path (engram_lost_move). TermAl keeps presuming the shell where it was, which can credit or bound wrongly. Pre-existing: found out of scope by the Claude reviewer of PI-26a round 2 (delegation-e3533fd0, session-8362, 2026-09-28), not introduced by that change.
acceptance: A line whose quoting TermAl cannot read the same way under every shell it may run in counts as a change TermAl cannot follow (Lost, and unbounded for write places), rather than as no change

engram_shell_commands (or its successor) honours a backslash escape outside quotes the way bash does, so `echo \"; cd /x; echo \"` is read as three commands, the second a cd; a regression test covers the followed and the lost reading of such a line
